text:
jess: Heads up — after yesterday's tensor-pool refactor we saw a spike in OOMs on the canary serving cluster for long-chat workloads. stack traces point at logits scratchpad allocations racing with reuse, and profiler shows bigger transient workspace during kernel-selection.

omar: Ugh. I noticed a perf regression too (p50 latency +12%). Might be the pool returning buffers before all async kernels finish. :eyes:

lee: Can you paste the stack traces / alloc logs? I want to see which allocator path is failing (freelist vs slab).

jess: Pasting a trimmed log:

```
2026-02-12T09:15:22Z ERROR OOM: allocate(activation_scratch, 72MB) failed
  at gpu::allocator::alloc_slab(..)
  ... serving::scratchpad::reuse() -> returned stale ptr 0x7fab3b8
  kernel-launch async stream 2 still using buffer
```

sasha: That 'stale ptr' bit smells like ownership handshake missing between request lifetime and pool recycle. We reused in-place because it reduced mallocs, but didn't fence with stream/event.

arjun: Also see this in profiler: workspace peaks when kernel selection chooses fused-attn for seq_len>2048 but batching heuristic increases effective seq because of padding. So requested workspace > reserved -> allocator falls back to a new temp buf.

katie: Quick numbers from Canary A vs B:
- before refactor: OOMs=0/24h, p50=45ms
- after refactor: OOMs=7/24h, p50=50ms, tail spikes at 750ms

omar: Proposed fix: add explicit CUDA event-based ownership handshake before returning buffer to pool. Flow:
1) allocate or reuse buffer
2) record stream/event on buffer when kernels submit
3) on buffer return, wait for event or mark as in-flight and only recycle after event completes

lee: Agree. We should avoid blocking CPU wait on event for the common fast path. Use deferred reclamation queue polled by a background thread that reclaims when events complete.

sasha: Also need to address logits scratchpad aliasing. We had an optimization to share logits buffer across batched micro-requests when shapes matched; but KV cache evictions plus variable decode lengths cause overlaps.

arjun: Two orthogonal things:
- ownership handshake to prevent early reuse (fixes OOM/double-use)
- smarter sizing: compute worst-case per-batch workspace based on kernel-selection + padding and reserve that on request to avoid transient alloc churn

jess: I sketched a patch: https://phabricator.redwood/infr/PR-1287 (WIP). Key parts:
- Buffer struct gets "inflight_event_id" and "return_epoch"
- Pool has reclaim queue -> background thread polls events via cuEventQuery
- When kernel selection changes workspace size, we attempt to resize in-pool buffer (grow) else fall back to a temporary allocation and record metric pool_temp_alloc

```
// pseudo
if (buf.size >= needed) return buf;
if (buf.try_grow(needed)) return buf;
else {
  metric.increment("pool_temp_alloc");
  return allocator.alloc(needed);
}
```

arjun: Love the metric. Add a per-model label and kernel-selection label so we can correlate with the perf regression dashboards.

katie: Can we add a canary flag to force the old behavior (no inheritance) so we can A/B quickly? Also want an alert if pool_temp_alloc > 0.5% of requests for a minute.

omar: I've run a unit test for stream-fence reclaim. Results: no regressions, but small CPU overhead ~0.4% due to background poller. Worth it for safety.

lee: Micro-bench: patched canary (with handshake + grow) on decoders with long sequences: p50 restored, OOMs eliminated in 48h test. One remaining tail spike traced to KV cache eviction path copying hidden state into a temp buffer while pool was busy.

sasha: For KV cache: we should prefer pre-allocated reserve per-request for copy-on-evict instead of allocating on-the-fly. Add a small per-request scratchpad (configurable) that lives for decode lifetime and is returned via handshake.

arjun: That ties into batching heuristics: if batcher pads to max seen seq in micro-batch, reserved per-request scratchpads add up. We need to update batching to expose actual effective sequence lengths so the allocator can compute accurate reservation.

katie: Action items:
- jess: land handshake + reclaim queue WIP, add metrics pool_temp_alloc (model,kernel)
- lee: add optional grow-in-place + test harness for kernel-selection sizing
- sasha: KV cache reserve proposal PR
- omar: run 72h canary and collect p50/p95/oom, set alert

jess: I'll push the WIP for review today. Plan to hotfix if canary looks good. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-canary started for shard-3 at 2026-02-12T13:02:00Z

omar: Noted. We'll watch dashboards and flag if pool_temp_alloc spikes. :eyes:
